about: Park directories of large cities and counties for hoop_pipeline.websources expand. Each entry: start_urls (a directory page or the site's sitemap.xml), park_link (regex for park-page URLs), optional next_link (regex for pagination / A-Z listing pages), bbox [west, south, east, north] for name matching, or pages (single pages fetched as they are, e.g. an amenity chart). Found by hand on 2026-10-17 through the polite fetcher (robots.txt honoured). Sites that refused us (robots 403, bot challenge) are listed under 'not_usable' with the reason.

directories.notes: 451 park pages; amenities are icons with data-key attributes.
92 Park Finder pages from the sitemap (the listing pages with form buttons).
285 park pages from the sitemap.
Partial: about 90 facilities (rec centers, pools, some parks).
135 park pages from the sitemap.
73 pages from the sitemap (a few venues too).
118 facility pages (parks, pools, community centers).
158 park pages; robots.txt Crawl-delay 10 is honoured.
Partial: 19 major city parks (the full ParkFinder answers robots.txt with 403).
No per-park pages; amenity charts on two pages.

181 park pages on /parks/ (180 in parks-sitemap.xml). Fall Creek & 30th: 'two renovated basketball courts' (count=2). Wes Montgomery: 'basketball pavilion' lines but judge_page says open_gym/court=False. 50 family centers at /facilities/<slug>/ not included.

19 links: community and regional parks have their own pages, but the ~135 neighborhood parks are only on the single neighborhood-parks page (one name heading plus amenity line each, many with 'Basketball court'), so it needs row-level extraction. Rampart and Monument Valley list basketball. sitemap.xml is paginated and mostly news.

No per-park pages. One table page holds all ~100 parks as 'Name Address | acres, amenities' rows, e.g. 'City Park 9701 E. 16th Ave. | basketball courts (2)'. It needs row-level extraction; park_link only matches the page's link to itself.

Covers only the 14 regional/riverfront parks. Erma Henderson: 'basketball courts'. Farwell's page is a construction update with no basketball. About 300 neighborhood parks exist only as /taxonomy/term/<id> pages with no listing, and robots.txt blocks sitemap.xml?page=N.

293 park pages. Amenities are icons only: . Watkins Regional shows the line 'Icon of a basketball.', but judge_page says court=False; the parser should map that alt text or the img title. Cosca: no basketball. The homepage has thousands of event links, so use the sitemap.

Regional parks are at /recreation-parks/parks/<slug>. The community-parks listing (?page=0..23, 5 parks per page) links mostly to /locations/<slug> pages with a 'Park Amenities' list. Lake Waterford: 'tennis or basketball courts'. Bay Head, Arnold and Beachwood: no basketball. The site's sitemap.xml is empty.
108 parks. Fairground and O'Fallon have basketball lines; Willmore has none. Ground truth: index.cfm?action=filterByAmenity&amenitySubType=42 lists the 33 parks with basketball courts.

77 Cincinnati Parks pages plus 22 CRC recreation centers; cincinnatiparks.com redirects here. Ziegler Park: 'Basketball Courts'. Inwood: none. Bond Hill CRC: 'Basketball (icon)'. CRC outdoor courts are only on the JS map at sports-field-or-court.
86 park and trail pages. Amenities are an icon list ('Basketball Half Court'). Diamond and Bella Vista: yes. Marshall: none. An amenities-sitemap.xml also exists.

Park pages sit at root slugs mixed with generic pages, so the regex is name-based (110 matches, with some '-2' duplicates). Jesse Owens and East Rancho Dominguez: outdoor and indoor basketball court. Roy Campanella: 'basketball court'. Athens: none. Nature centers and wildlife sanctuaries are excluded.

Only 24 recreation centers plus 2 parks (Joaquin Miller, Lakeside) have pages; most city parks have none. The hub page links all 24 rec centers, while the Recreation-Centers list uses ASP.NET postback paging. Amenities are in ul.venue-feature-list. Arroyo Viejo: 'Basketball Court'. Brookdale: 'Full-size basketball courts'. The first parse of Arroyo returned 0 lines and a refetch was fine, so this may be flaky.
